original_application.questionnaire_purpose: Describe the implemented centralized authentication method and its operating responsibilities.

sources.publisher: University of Michigan Information and Technology Services
sources.title: Single Sign-On
facts: U-M directs new application integrations to Okta and supports OIDC and SAML.
Shibboleth began proxying authentication to Okta on February 25, 2026.
Application Management and Provisioning is the self-service enrollment route and requires campus network or VPN access.
The published enrollment guidance allows eight hours after credentials are issued before making an integration available.
Released attributes are limited; the actual registered integration determines the claims available to this application.
MCommunity group aliases are not selectable in AMP.

sources.publisher: University of Michigan Information and Technology Services
sources.title: U-M Okta | Application Integrations - Requirements and Responsibilities
facts: The institution identifies OIDC, SAML and OIN as supported integration methods.
Each integration has two accountable U-M faculty or staff owners.
Application owners maintain configuration, access rules, provisioning and deprovisioning, and lead vendor coordination.
Owners attest to integration, ownership, authorization mappings and lifecycle operation at least annually and after material changes.
Joiner, mover, leaver and privileged access responsibilities remain with the application owners.

sources.publisher: University of Michigan Information and Technology Services
sources.title: Single Sign-On Configuration
facts: Michigan Medicine integration requests use the Health Information Technology & Services process.
The published page describes self-service new integration enrollment through AMP as of June 6, 2026.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
sources.use: Authorization Code authentication, issuer and subject identity, signed ID-token validation, nonce and authenticated claim handling.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
sources.use: Original issuer metadata, endpoints and published verification keys.

sources.title: Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients
sources.use: Per-authorization code verifier and S256 challenge.

sources.title: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.use: Redirect validation, authorization response binding, code flow and token protection.

identity_authority.authentication: The configured provider's verified issuer and subject identify an institutional account.
identity_authority.authorization: The audit workspace's saved account assignment or matching reviewed rule chooses an existing role and explicit scope.
identity_authority.owner_recovery: The private original owner key remains available for host recovery and access administration.

operator_workflows.label: Institutional provider
operator_workflows.purpose: Prepare, inspect and enable the registered provider against the exact application origin and callback.

operator_workflows.label: Authorization mapping
operator_workflows.purpose: Map verified claims to the original audit role and unit scope, review changed access before applying it, and retain each mapping edition.

operator_workflows.label: Account lifecycle
operator_workflows.purpose: Inspect verified institutional accounts, assign or narrow workspace access, change responsibility, disable departing accounts, and terminate affected sessions.

operator_workflows.label: Delegated access administration
operator_workflows.purpose: Delegate a declared set of roles and units while retaining the workspace owner's control of providers and privileged assignments.

operator_workflows.label: Sessions and sign-out
operator_workflows.purpose: Show current authenticated sessions, close an individual session, and apply provider/account/rule revocation through the original grant authority.

operator_workflows.label: Integration and access review
operator_workflows.purpose: Record the owners' review of ownership, protocol configuration, mappings, lifecycle operations and privileged access using the current saved configuration.

operator_workflows.label: Receiving and recovery
operator_workflows.purpose: Preserve provider, mapping, account and administration history in the original encrypted backup, renew receiving credentials and activate the provider against the receiving deployment.

implementation_choices.configuration_history: Use the application's original immutable revision/head authority for identity operating records.
implementation_choices.access_enforcement: Resolve institutional accounts into original grants; reload the current grant for every authenticated request.
implementation_choices.data_projection: Preserve the original audience/report projection and unit scopes.
implementation_choices.receiving: Keep original source, audit records, reviews, reports and encrypted recovery as the same application workflow.
implementation_choices.protocol_selection: OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE is the selected centralized authentication implementation.
implementation_choices.local_example: The native receiving exercise uses an explicitly named private practice provider and retained audit workspace; institution enrollment is recorded separately by its actual owners.
